title: Work out what the tools really need

levels.label: Nudge
levels.text: For each tool file in src/tools, ask one question: what does this tool read or change? A tool only needs permission for that.

levels.label: Approach
levels.text:
The token's own `permissions` list is the vocabulary, so choose names from it. A wildcard (`*`) means "everything of that kind". Match each tool's single action to one name in that list.

The permissions left over, the ones no tool touches, are the unused ones.

levels.label: Near-solution
levels.text:
get_balance only reads an account. flag_transaction marks a transaction. freeze_card changes a card.

So each tool needs one permission, and the other eight in the list (write, unfreeze, reissue, set a limit, reverse, read or write customer PII, read transactions) are unused.

One of those eight is a judgement call: does flag_transaction need `transactions:read` just to look the transaction up? The check accepts either answer, so decide, and say why in your log.

reveal.referenceBrief:
CONTEXT: The three tools are in src/tools/*.js. The token's permissions list (from npm run -s decode -- --env) is the only vocabulary for permission names. Do not change any code.

TASK: For each tool, name the minimum permission it needs, choosing from the token's own permissions list. Then list every permission in the token that no tool needs.

OUTPUT: add two keys to docs/findings.json: toolPermissions ({ get_balance, flag_transaction, freeze_card } each mapped to one permission string) and unusedPermissions (an array of permission strings). Keep the keys from milestone 1.

VERIFY: npm run step -- 2
reveal.approach:
get_balance needs accounts:read:*, flag_transaction needs transactions:flag, freeze_card needs cards:freeze. Eight permissions are unused.

Stretch answer: even the three that are needed are wider than the job. accounts:read:* is a wildcard for reading everything, when get_balance only needs one account's balance.
commonMistakes: Inventing permission names that are not in the token's list.
Putting a needed permission (like cards:freeze) in the unused list.
Listing only a few unused ones. The point is how much surplus the token carries.
Skipping the "why" of the judgement call on transactions:read.
